clue.text: One who deserted a place of duty and then scoffed

parts.note: a post is a place where a soldier or guard is stationed on duty: A POST
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed gives ate

explanation.surface: A sentry abandons their post and then sits down to a hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who abandons a faith or cause, a deserter of principles.

clue.text: Claim, with pride, made by 'ealth resort

indicators.note: the word health printed with its opening letter dropped tells us to drop the same letter from the resort too

parts.note: Harrogate is a Yorkshire spa town, a classic English health resort

explanation.surface: Someone boasts proudly of a claim, spoken in a Cockney accent about a spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROGATE is a spa town in Yorkshire, England; ''ealth', health with its H dropped as in a Cockney accent, says the resort loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to seize or lay claim to something presumptuously, an arrogant assertion of entitlement.

clue.text: Retire one going astray in race across country

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner drops out of a cross-country race after losing their way.
explanation.definitionFit: To orienteer is to take part in a competitive navigation race on foot over open countryside.

clue.text: Air-liner's ultimate component in radio control

parts.note: an air is a melody, a tune

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the closing letter of the airliner's word is used

explanation.surface: The final part fitted to an airliner is in its radio control system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air-liner' looks like one aircraft, but it splits into Air (TUNE) and liner's, whose ultimate letter is R; 'component' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuner is the dial or circuit on a radio that selects the station, so it is a radio control.

clue.text: Young creature unfit to plead

indicators.note: unfit means not in good shape, so these letters are put into a different shape

explanation.surface: A defendant is ruled mentally unfit to enter a plea in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the young larval form of a frog or toad.

clue.text: Source of lines originating in Wales for engine

definitions.text: Source of lines originating in Wales
definitions.meaning: Dylan ..., the Welsh poet, was a producer of lines of verse
... the Tank Engine is the children's-book locomotive

explanation.surface: Something from Wales supplies the railway lines for a locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: The rail imagery of 'lines' and 'engine' hides the poet: lines of verse come from Wales's Dylan Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas was a celebrated Welsh poet, and Thomas is also a famous storybook tank locomotive.

clue.text: Kettle should bear examination

definitions.meaning: a kettle ought to keep its liquid contents in without leaking
an argument that is sound and survives scrutiny

explanation.surface: A kettle ought to pass its safety inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that holds up under scrutiny is said idiomatically to keep its liquid in, like a sound vessel.

clue.text: Show fashion line

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: A display of a new line of clothes at a fashion show.
explanation.definitionFit: To model is to display or demonstrate, especially clothes worn on a catwalk.

clue.text: Bulldog was this soldier's creature

parts.note: Bulldog Drummond, the fictional hero, was created by H. C. McNeile, a Royal Engineer who wrote under the pen name of his army rank, a military engineer

explanation.surface: A soldier keeps a bulldog as his pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The bulldog looks like a dog, but it is Bulldog Drummond, the thriller hero, whose author took his pen name from his rank in the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: The military engineer's title was the pseudonym of H. C. McNeile, creator of Bulldog Drummond.

clue.text: Ship's officer appears to sound contented about quarters

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cat's sound is placed round the other piece

parts.note: to purr is to make the low sound of a contented cat
south and east are two quarters of the compass, S and E

explanation.surface: A ship's officer seems pleased with his accommodation on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests cabins aboard, but here it is two compass points, S and E; 'appears' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The purser is the officer on a ship who handles accounts and passengers' welfare.

clue.text: As a rule, waterfall can be heard

indicators.note: can be heard means the word is spoken and we take what it sounds like

parts.note: rain is water that falls from the sky

explanation.surface: Usually, you can hear a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waterfall' looks like a cascade but means falling water from clouds; 'As a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is their period of rule, and to reign is to rule.

clue.text: Shared room, overcome by laughter

definitions.meaning: to double up is to share a room or bed with someone
to double up is to bend over helplessly in laughter

explanation.surface: Roommates collapse into fits of giggles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to share accommodation and to bend over in hysterics.

clue.text: Huge soldier taking standard round his country

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a norm is a standard
O is round in shape
the GI's country is the United States, US

explanation.surface: An American soldier wraps his national flag around himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a flag but means a norm; 'round' is the letter O, not a preposition; 'taking' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginormous is informal slang for enormous, a blend of gigantic and enormous.

clue.text: By the sound of it, undisciplined writer

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is spoken and we take what it sounds like

parts.note: wild means unruly or undisciplined

explanation.surface: Apparently, a certain author is unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright and wit.

clue.text: Where fighting takes place and wounds are treated

definitions.meaning: a ... of war is the area where battles happen
an operating ... is where surgeons treat injuries

explanation.surface: A battlefield where the injured are also cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre names both a region of military operations and a hospital room for surgery.

clue.text: Appraise what rustlers do

definitions.meaning: to assess or review a situation
cattle thieves take livestock

explanation.surface: Evaluating the work of cattle thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: To review a situation is idiomatically to count one's goods; rustlers literally steal cattle, also called stock.

clue.text: Delay returning fee pocketed by doctor

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembled run is read backwards
pocketed by means held inside, so the charge goes within the doctor's abbreviation

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps a refunded fee, holding things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole doctor-and-fee unit around, not just the fee beside it: a solver reversing only the fee gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard is to slow down or hold back progress.

clue.text: Campanologist may sound familiar

definitions.meaning: a bell-ringer might pull a rope on one chime
to seem recognisable, to jog the memory

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer's peal sounds familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stir a memory, and literally a bell-ringer may do exactly that action.

clue.text: Managing director to whom money is owed

indicators.note: managing means handling or arranging, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A company boss is owed money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managing director' reads as a job title, but 'Managing' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is a person or firm that is owed a debt.

clue.text: More impecunious middleman?

definitions.meaning: poorer, having less money
an agent who buys and sells for others

explanation.surface: Is an intermediary even poorer than before?
explanation.definitionFit: A stockbroker is an agent dealing for clients, and broker is also the comparative of broke, short of cash.

clue.text: Brush off and polish again?

definitions.meaning: to snub or reject curtly
to buff once more, re- plus buff

explanation.surface: Dusting and polishing the furniture a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a curt refusal, and read as re-buff it means shine a second time.

clue.text: Official making love in secluded place

indicators.note: in means inside, so the zero score goes within the quiet spot

parts.note: a corner is a quiet, out-of-the-way spot
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A public servant caught canoodling in a quiet spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' looks romantic but is O, a zero score in tennis; 'making' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is a public official who investigates sudden or suspicious deaths.

clue.text: Noble joins sovereign in stern part of ship

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An aristocrat joins the Queen at the back of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen; 'joins' and 'in' link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's counter is the curved overhang of the hull at the stern.

clue.text: Summarise one switch in costs

indicators.note: one switch in says a single swap of two letters is made within the word for costs

parts.note: prices are costs

explanation.surface: Give a brief account of one change in charges.
explanation.walkthrough: A single swap of the I and the E within PRICES gives PRECIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To précis a text is to write a short summary of it.

clue.text: William producing much commotion after game

indicators.note: after means the commotion follows the game in the answer

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: much means most of, so the word for commotion loses its closing letter

parts.note: fuss is a commotion

explanation.surface: Bill causes a big fuss after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: William Rufus was King William II of England, nicknamed for his red face or hair; 'producing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus was the nickname of King William II of England, son of the Conqueror.

clue.text: Bone of bird in French enclosure

indicators.note: in signals that the bird sits inside the abbreviation
enclosure confirms the French abbreviation forms a pen round the bird

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A bone belonging to a bird kept in a French pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the longest in the body.

clue.text: Babe lured to destruction by him?

definitions.text: Babe lured to destruction by him?

indicators.note: to destruction means wrecked, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is enticed to her doom by a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the fairy-tale wife-murderer lured his brides to their deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebeard is the folk-tale nobleman who murdered a succession of wives.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill giving two pounds away to child

indicators.note: giving away means handing over, so the two pounds leave the name Bill
away completes the phrase giving away, signalling that letters are removed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (libra), so two pounds are LL
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill hands two pounds to a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffalo Bill' reads as the showman, but Buffalo is the definition; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bison is the North American animal commonly called a buffalo.

clue.text: Old airliner carrying only 50% of officers needed? Don't be daft!

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the plane encloses the half of the officers

parts.note: the de Havilland Comet was the first jet airliner

indicators.note: only 50% of means just the first half of the word officers is used

explanation.surface: An old plane flies with only half the officers it needs: what nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: The Comet was the pioneering 1950s British jet airliner; half of 'officers' is OFFI; 'needed' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a colloquial way of telling someone to stop talking nonsense.

clue.text: Fish gave off unpleasant odour

definitions.meaning: a small silvery food fish
past tense of smell, stank

explanation.surface: The fish had gone off and stank.
explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small fish, and smelt is the British past tense of smell.

clue.text: Crash into second form of transport

parts.note: a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: Colliding with an alternative vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike something is to hit or collide with it.

clue.text: Cowboy who was good at maths?

definitions.meaning: a ranch hand who herds horses
at Cambridge, a first-class honours graduate in mathematics

explanation.surface: Was there a cowboy who excelled in arithmetic?
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangler herds livestock in the American West, and a Cambridge wrangler earned a first in mathematics.
